title: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
text: I hated Dark Souls 2 when it originally came out, with a passion, it did not live up to the amazing experience that was DS 1, specifically the world of Drangleic. However, in 2017, I can very much say, to the extent of with pride, that this game is worth playing, it's much better than the original release. It still does not, in my opinion, live up to the uniqueness if DS1, that game will never be surpassed, even with it's flaws, but it doesn't change the fact that this, DS2, is a good game. I'm not going to say the level design is better than DS1, because I've only put 13 hours in, but it feels much less intimidating than DS1, and that's not necessarily bad, it makes me want to explore it, and not worry about completing it, in DS1, even now, after 6 years of playing it, a game that I can run through easily, still intimidates me, I just want to go to the bosses, and move on, so I personally like the invitingness of DS2 more. The level design, while seemingly less intimidating, doesn't negate from the difficulty, I was able to breeze through almost all of Dark Souls 3, but this game makes me question my skill, perhaps the combat encounters are in actuality, more dangerous than in DS3? Different devs would explain this. My gripes with the game, lie in the controls, and movement, I dislike the running, it did not need to be changed from DS1, it was fine the way it was, it's slugish and stiff. Speaking of stiff, the combat in this game is a lot more stiff than in DS1 and 3, you feel very stocky, everything you do seems to get you stuck to the ground, or in an animation for a brief second, long enough for you to notice it and slightly annoy you. It feels a lot less fluid than in DS1. This however, doesn't make me not want to play the game, it's not a big enough of an annoyance to even make me think to stop playing. This game is very much worth the humbly modest asking price of $40, however, like all other games, I suggest waiting for a sale. But, if you want to support FromSoft, don't hesitate to pay full price. Your money will have been well spent.

title: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
text: How do you make a sequel to a memetic masterpiece? Let alone Dark Souls? After many playthroughs of the first game, I can see why From didn't just go "ok heres more of Dark Souls 1 but with polish" like they did with Artorias. That would have been to familiar, too comfortable, and that goes against the point of the franchise. 2 is inferior to 1, but in a way that creates a haunting, surreal, and uncomfortable experience, which is powerful in it's own way. It's like Dark Souls was recollected in a fever dream, which is almost aggressive in how little sense it makes (windmill elevator, you'll know what I mean). The engine has been improved in small ways, but the combat (at least early on) is deliberately sluggish and many of the tactics that were so strong in the first game have been stripped away. If this appeals, play the Scholar version of 2. If you care more about gameplay, or just want more of the first Dark Souls, skip to 3.

title: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
text: This is a game that I keep wanting to LOVE. The story is interesting (despite what some people say about it not fitting the rest of the series), and I find the characters intriguing enough that I can stay in character. As a sorcoress, I feel like I have UNGODLY AMOUNTS OF POWER... and that even that much power is just not quite enough. It has it's faults, though; and they are some real whoppers. * If you have never played a Souls game, prepare to buy replacement controllers every time you get into an area that requires jumping. The jump mechanics of ALL these games are crap. * In this game, the healing flask is abysmally slow. Better off using purchasable healing gems all the time. * The one really huge downside is the layout. The world map in Dark Souls 2 was designed by a pack of tindalos' hounds. Say you are running along the edge of the ocean with the water on your left... you pass through a tunnel that curves left, and come out into dense forest that curves slightly left... by the time you reach the end of the forest ruins, a part of you, deep down inside, is convinced that you should be a mile out at sea. And lets not get into the part where you take an elevator up near the top of a huge tower, and come out from underground at ground level, into a volcanic crater... It IS a good game. It should have been a lot better. Personally, noted issues aside, I do highly recommend it.

title: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin
text: People complain a lot about this one not being as good as the first. Lets look at it differently: Dark Souls 2 has all the visuals that we desired from the first. Sure it doesn't have the compelling story like its predecessor, nor an infamous character like Solaire, but all sequels have never been as popular as the first. Dark Souls 2 may not be the best game, but I don't regret a single minute I put into this game. The DLC's are all amazing, some of the battles being the toughest and most interesting throughout the game. The menus and massive amounts of armor choices are somewhat confusing, that would be my only complaint. All acheivments can be unlocked via NG++ just like the first, so it really isn't a let down like some players blow it up to be. If you've heard bad things about this game, shrug them off and try it for yourself.

text: Genre - Japanese 3D Fighting Game (with very sexy girls in skimpy outfits) I have played DOA games before on the XBox and although they aren't as good as  some other fighting games, they offer enough to make them interesting and fun, and this game is no different. On writing this review we were still missing achievements and a multiplayer mode. However, I have played the story mode extensively and tried arcade mode with a few characters. The visuals look great and the fighting is smooth. You don't have as many of the crazy moves of other fighting games and have to rely mostly on kicks and punches. However, the fights are still highly enjoyable with different difficulty modes to play. There are many characters to choose from and you can also play in tag team mode. The story mode was highly enjoyable and fairly immersive, although it won't win any oscars. You can buy more costumes at quite a premium rate. However, maybe they will become more reasonable in the sale, If not you would have to be a die hard fan to get them. title: DOOM
text: Great stuff all around. Doom 2016 is not a pure return to form - while original games had open mazelike levels with pre-placed monsters, this sequel presents most combat encounters arena-FPS style: player is locked in an area until everybody else is dead. This does not hamper the exploration though, and there's a lot of nifty little secrets to find. So, SP campaign is great and is decently long(took me around 14 hours to beat). It also sports a surprisingly developed story and lore, which are also really easy to ignore if you don't care. Soundtrack is praised all over the Internet, and for good reason. Combat is fast and brutal with a very heavy emphasis on mobility, and has a refreshing amount of verticality to it. Progression systems are in there and provide a healthy amount of variety and empowerment creep. Even checkpoint placement feels right. Game also looks good, runs great, and is also very scalable to boot, providing a generous amount of settings. I'm having trouble thinking of any technical faults, except maybe that some settings make very little visual difference going even from low to Ultra, while still causing a performance hit(Setting shadows from ultra to nightmare leads to a huge FPS drop, but the difference is barely visible even on screenshots). But at any rate, it's reasonably easy to run on 60+ FPS on most modenr hardware configurations. So is there anything wrong with it? Yes. Multiplayer is meh. It does have a lot of content: multiple game modes, lots of maps, tons of customization options, vast array of stuff to unlock. And maybe it is the problem - from the get go a lot of stuff is locked and has to be unlocked by achieving levels and completing challenges. Loadout system and two-weapon limit does not help either. It's not that those systems are inherently wrong, but they just feel out of place in this title. So overall? If you are an FPS fan with any amount of self-respect, go and get it. It is really, really good.

title: DRAGON QUEST HEROES™ II
text: Comparing Dragon Quest Heroes 2 to other Warriors style games: DQH2 has more story.  This can be good or bad, depending on your preference.  I found myself enjoying the admittedly simple storyline, and the option to skip cutscenes exists for those who don't. DQH2 is more challenging.  In most other Warriors style games, powerful enemies are merely opposing generals.  Their movesets will be comparable to your own, meaning they will require a large stat advantage to make them challenging to fight due to the fact that a player will generally be superior to the AI in terms of skill.  In DQH2 Heroes, the powerful enemies are monsters with bodies and movesets that differ drastically from the heroes.  This, along with the fact that you are much more often pit against multiple powerful enemies than in other Warriors games, brings the difficulty in line with what one might expect from a traditional ARPG.  This leads into the next point... DQH2 has more RPG style features:  levelling, buying equipment, side-quests, the ability to travel anywhere in the world you currently have access to rather than just the next battle. Those who played the previous DQ games will appreciate the nostalgia appeal, as many of the playable fighters are heroes from previous games.  They also come with remixes of their original theme music from those games. Battles with defeatable allies can be frustrating, as your allies will generally be far more helpless than in other Warriors style games. Overall, this is an excellent game that will apeal to many more gamers than just Warriors fans.  Anyone who likes ARPGs will be able to enjoy DQH2.  I can recommed this one generally to anyone who wants a fun but challenging romp through hordes of monsters.

If you love hack and slash (think Dynasty Warriors, albeit without the agressive hordes, you can mostly just walk past them without a hitch until the story forced combat, which mostly ignore you anyway but you must protect someone) with the ability to change your class like the original Final Fantasy, then this is for you. The combat is great if you don't have it on the simplistic setting. Keayboard and mouse are definitely on the back burner, as well as controller support for Logitech Dual Action controllers. Expect to spend time in the menu to figure out what key goes with what ported controller button.
